templates.text: The lungs show robust surfactant production, though the gut's peristaltic waves are still somewhat immature and disorganized.
Cardiac septation is complete with strong valve formation, yet the renal tubules lag slightly in concentrating ability.
Neurologically, primitive reflexes are present and brisk, but the suck-swallow-breathe coordination requires a brief {delay} second pause to synchronize.
Hepatic enzyme systems are coming online, while the pancreatic islet cells are still finalizing their insulin secretory rhythm.
The cry is strong and lusty, yet the thermoregulatory response to cooling is a fraction slower than expected.
Muscle tone is generally good, though extensor patterns momentarily dominate before yielding to flexion.
Auditory startle is robust and consistent, contrasting with visual tracking that is present but jerky and unsustained.
The skin barrier is functionally intact, but eccrine sweat gland activity remains patchy and inconsistent.
Bone ossification centers are developing on schedule, while the cartilage of the external ear remains unusually pliable.
Gastrointestinal motility is present, yet the migrating motor complex cycles are shorter and less regular.
The adrenal cortex produces adequate cortisol, but its diurnal rhythm is not yet firmly established.
Respiratory drive is strong, though the intercostal muscles show slight fatigue during prolonged crying jags.
The Babinski reflex is clearly present, while the palmar grasp lacks the full, sustained strength of a term infant.
Renal blood flow and filtration are adequate, but tubular reabsorption of sodium is marginally less efficient.
The initial cry is vigorous, but its acoustic modulation shows less variation in pitch and harmonic structure.
Hematopoiesis is active in the bone marrow, though reticulocyte counts sit at the lower end of the normal range.
The pupillary light reflex is prompt and equal, but accommodation to near objects is sluggish and incomplete.
Liver conjugation pathways are operational, leading to a mild, transient elevation in unconjugated bilirubin.
The Moro reflex is complete but asymmetrical, with one arm often adducting more forcefully than the other.
Cardiac output is sufficient, yet the ductus arteriosus demonstrates a pronounced murmur before full closure.
Swallowing is effective, but the gag reflex is almost hyper-reactive, triggering easily with minimal stimulation.
The rooting reflex is easily elicited, though the subsequent latch is sometimes shallow and requires repositioning.
Thermoregulation is functional in a neutral environment, but brown adipose tissue metabolism is slower to activate.
The acoustic cry analysis shows good intensity, but the phonation is breathier with less clear harmonic bands.
Peripheral perfusion is good, though capillary refill time is consistently at the upper limit of normal.
The plantar grasp is firm, in contrast to the stepping reflex which is present but poorly coordinated and staggering.
Gastric emptying proceeds, yet pyloric sphincter tone is variable, leading to occasional non-bilious spit-ups.
The auditory system localizes sound, but the orienting response is delayed by roughly {seconds} seconds.
Myelination of major motor tracts is progressing, while fine distal nerve conduction velocities are slightly delayed.
Overall tone favors flexion, yet the infant periodically arches into brief, unsustained opisthotonic postures.
